about.title: Fountain Valley Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Fountain Valley residents rely on nearby clinics and hospital campuses along corridors like Brookhurst and Euclid for everything from routine visits to urgent care. Most of the time, that care meets the standard patients expect. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication errors cause harm, the effects can be lasting. California law treats these claims differently than typical injury cases — under MICRA, there are strict notice requirements, tight filing deadlines, and specific rules about expert testimony. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove malpractice; establishing a deviation from the accepted standard of care usually requires a qualified medical expert. Our team reviews the details of your situation, explains the MICRA framework as it applies to your claim, and advises on next steps — free of charge and without any obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Fountain Valley Patients Choose Us

items.title: Understanding MICRA's Tight Timeline
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice notice within one year of discovering the harm, capped at three years from the injury, plus a mandatory 90-day pre-suit notice period. Our team helps track these deadlines correctly.

items.title: Navigating the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: MICRA sets a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts annually by statute. We're familiar with the current cap amount and can help set realistic expectations about your claim.

items.title: Securing a Qualified Medical Expert
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't evidence of malpractice, California claims almost always need a qualified medical expert to establish a standard-of-care violation. We know how to build that foundation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice before filing. Our team can review your specific dates to determine where you stand.

items.question: Does a bad result from surgery or treatment mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, not just that the outcome was disappointing or unexpected. This is typically established through a qualified medical expert's review of the records.

items.question: Are there local factors in Fountain Valley that matter for these claims?
items.answer: Fountain Valley's medical facilities serve a community of nearly 57,000 people, and claims can involve care given at clinics or hospitals near corridors like Brookhurst or Euclid. We review where and when the care was provided as part of building your claim.
